items.headline: Anthropic's IPO prospectus discloses $518bn in AI infrastructure commitments and a $42bn net loss
items.note: Prospectus seeks a $2tn+ valuation on revenue of $4.6bn and an operating loss over $8bn, against $518bn of infrastructure obligations to Google ($111.1bn), Amazon ($110bn), Microsoft ($31.4bn) and Broadcom ($161.2bn) — the circular compute-for-equity financing the essay title describes. Nvidia's separately reported anchor-investor talks (Reuters, 12 Sep) reinforce the fit. Also touches 'What the 10-K can't see' as a secondary angle on off-balance-sheet AI spend.

items.headline: Stanford/King's College London study: AI-adopting firms shed junior headcount even as senior hiring grows
items.note: Chandar (Stanford) and Klein Teeselink (King's College London) analysed 1.25bn job postings and 154m employment records across 41 countries: senior roles up 6.7%, junior roles down 3% at AI-adopting firms; 22-25 year-olds in exposed roles 19% below expected employment. Direct evidentiary update to the essay's thesis, ~9 days old rather than breaking.

items.headline: Anthropic's Amodei calls on the AI industry to 'pace the frontier' on safety
items.note: Amodei's unilateral commitment to embed third-party evaluators (METR) with internal-team access, plus a call for industry coordination and a government-mediated safety waiver, reframes alignment as a resourcing decision rather than a research one. Altman echoed the commitment; picked up widely via AP syndication. Older story (18 days) and light on hard figures, so treat as a supporting angle rather than the trigger.

items.headline: Gartner: AI spending is outrunning the financial guardrails meant to control it
items.note: Gartner finds AI spend in customer-service functions up 38% against a 2% rise in overall function budgets, with only 44% of organisations having adopted AI FinOps/financial guardrails — 'shadow IT, priced in tokens.' Weaker corpus fit and a month old; worth a look only if the line needs a lighter CFO-mandate item this week.
